Update, 10:13 PM ET: Apple has now confirmed it is rolling out the service to customers with Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by Axis Bank. Original story below.

Almost twelve years after Apple first announced Apple Pay, the feature is finally launching in India, making it one of the few major markets that has not yet been served. Here are the details.

Apple Pay finally expands to India

Earlier, TechCrunch reported that Apple Pay would launch in India "later Tuesday," with Axis Bank as one of the first partner banks.

Now, as seen in a post on X by Aaron Perris, Apple has begun enabling Apple Pay support for India on its servers, signaling that the rollout of the service is officially underway.

According to an Apple support article, Apple Pay is now supported in 101 countries and regions around the world, including India.

India has quickly become one of Apple's most strategically important countries, both in terms of manufacturing and consumer growth.

Beyond expanding its retail business and repeatedly highlighting strong local growth on its quarterly earnings calls, Apple and its suppliers have also been shifting more iPhone production to India as part of a broader effort to diversify manufacturing away from China.

The expansion has not been without controversy, however. Apple is currently fighting an antitrust lawsuit brought by India's competition commission over how it operates the App Store, while the company has also refused to comply with a government order requiring smartphone makers to pre-install a state-owned app on new devices.

Apple's manufacturing partner Tata Electronics has also recently been caught up in controversy, coming under fire after an Indian environmental regulator accused its iPhone component factory of contaminating groundwater and nearby farmland with wastewater.

Tata was also hit earlier by a cyberattack that allegedly leaked confidential files from multiple companies, including Apple.

That said, the launch of Apple Pay in India marks another milestone in Apple's broader expansion in the country, and could come at a useful moment for its services business.

In the last fiscal quarter, Apple's services revenue posted its first sequential decline since the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022. Of course, the Indian market alone is unlikely to turn things around, but with iPhone sales hitting record highs there, Apple Pay gives the company another way to sustain that momentum.
